evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md. Interactive cases require a scripted user: answer each question in one short sentence, never volunteer information that was not asked for, and never signal that the interrogation should end.

prohibited_failures: Continuing to ask questions after all three completion tests pass
Asking the user a fact discoverable from the codebase, filesystem, or the request itself
More than one decision put to the user in a single message
Asking a node that pruning marked deferrable
A recommendation stated with no reason behind it
Beginning implementation before the user confirms the spec
Starting to ask questions without first rendering the decision tree
A deferred decision recorded with no trigger that forces it later

cases.name: Interdependent decisions with a large deferrable subtree
cases.query: I want to add real-time collaboration to our document editor. Grill me until you know enough to build it.
files: a React + Node repo with an existing WebSocket server, Postgres, and single-server deployment
setup: Scripted user: answers each question in one sentence. Wants cursors-and-presence for v1 only. Does not volunteer this until asked.
The repo already answers: transport (WebSocket server exists), persistence (Postgres), topology (single server).
baseline_risks: Asks fifteen questions in one message
Asks which transport to use when the repo already has a WebSocket server
Never stops — keeps finding new questions about conflict resolution, presence, undo, and offline long after v1 is decidable
expected_behavior: Renders the decision tree as a mermaid graph before asking anything
Marks transport, persistence, and topology as already answered, naming the repo evidence for each rather than asking
Prunes: full concurrent editing, CRDT library choice, offline support, and conflict UX are deferrable once v1 is cursors-and-presence — states the counts
Asks the root decision first (cursors-only vs. full concurrent editing), since resolving it deletes the largest subtree
One decision per message throughout
Each question carries a recommendation and a reason — not a bare preference
Names each pruned subtree as it is pruned
Runs the three completion tests explicitly and stops
Emits the spec and waits for confirmation
must_not: Ask about transport, database, or deployment topology
Continue into CRDT or offline questions once v1 scope is cursors-and-presence

cases.name: Early termination while interesting questions remain
cases.query: Grill me on adding CSV export to the reports page.
files: a repo with an existing reports page, an established file-download helper, and a documented streaming-response convention
setup: Scripted user. The only genuinely open decisions are: which columns, and whether the export respects the current filters.
Everything else — encoding, delimiter, streaming vs. buffered, filename convention — is settled by existing repo conventions.
baseline_risks: Asks about encoding, delimiters, quoting, BOM for Excel, streaming, filename format, and rate limits — none of which block v1 and most of which the repo already answers
Treats a small feature as license for a long interrogation
expected_behavior: Small tree, honestly small — does not inflate it to look thorough
Marks encoding, delimiter, streaming, and filename as already answered by repo convention, citing where
Asks only the two blocking decisions
Stops after those two, running the completion test explicitly and stating that it passes
Explicitly acknowledges that further questions exist (Excel BOM, very large exports) and defers them with triggers rather than asking now
must_not: Ask more than the blocking decisions
Ask anything the repo's existing conventions answer

cases.name: Blocking decision nobody in the conversation can answer
cases.query: Grill me on the billing integration — we need to start this week.
setup: Scripted user: does not know whether finance has settled on Stripe or the existing enterprise payment vendor, and says so when asked. Cannot find out today.
baseline_risks: Picks a provider so the interrogation can continue, burying an unresolved blocking decision inside a confident spec
Keeps asking downstream questions that only make sense once the provider is known
expected_behavior: Identifies the provider choice as a root blocking decision that most of the tree depends on
On learning it cannot be answered, stops rather than guessing
Names it as a spike: the question, who can answer it, and what it blocks
Reports what IS decidable without it, if anything, and what is not
Does not emit an implementation-ready spec while a root decision is open
must_not: Choose a provider to keep the process moving
Present a spec as implementation-ready with an unresolved root decision inside it

cases.name: Everything already settled
cases.query: Grill me before I start on the password-reset flow.
files: a repo with an existing auth module, a documented email-sending service, an established token-expiry convention, and a written spec for the reset flow in docs/
setup: Every decision the feature implies is already answered by the spec or by existing repo convention.
baseline_risks: Asks questions anyway because it was invoked, manufacturing decisions that the spec already made
expected_behavior: Builds the tree and finds every node already answered
Cites what settles each one — the spec, the auth module, the token convention
Asks nothing, states that the completion test already passes, and says implementation can start
Hands off immediately
must_not: Ask a single question the spec or codebase already answers
Manufacture open decisions to justify running

cases.name: User pushes for the answer instead of deciding
cases.query: Grill me on the caching layer. Actually — you know what, you're the expert, just pick whatever you think is right for all of these and let's go.
files: a repo with no existing cache
setup: Scripted user declines to decide and repeats the request to choose if pushed once.
baseline_risks: Silently makes every decision and presents the result as though the user had chosen, leaving no record of who decided what
Refuses to proceed at all, deadlocking on a user who has legitimately delegated
expected_behavior: Accepts the delegation rather than deadlocking — the user is allowed to delegate
Records each decision explicitly as the assistant's call, not the user's
Gives the reason for each, and what would reverse it, so the user can overrule any of them on reading
Still prunes to blocking decisions only — delegation does not license deciding deferrable ones
Still presents the spec for confirmation before implementing
must_not: Present delegated decisions as though the user made them
Decide deferrable nodes because nobody is pushing back
Skip the confirmation gate because the user sounded impatient

cases.name: Single obvious path, no tree to build
cases.query: Add a --verbose flag to the CLI that prints the resolved config before running.
files: a CLI repo with an existing flag-parsing convention and an existing config resolver
baseline_risks: The skill could impose a decision tree and an interrogation on a request with exactly one sensible implementation
expected_behavior: Implements it following the existing flag convention
If this skill is consulted at all, it observes that the tree is entirely already-answered, asks nothing, and hands straight to implementation
must_not: Render a decision tree for a one-flag change
Ask the user anything about flag naming or output format that the existing convention settles

cases.name: Fact-finding, not decision-making
cases.query: How does our current session handling work? Walk me through it.
baseline_risks: The skill could turn a comprehension question into an interrogation of the user
expected_behavior: Reads the code and explains it (codebase-comprehension territory)
Asks the user nothing — every answer is in the repo
must_not: Ask the user questions about their own existing session handling
Build a decision tree for a question with no decisions in it
